title: Beatrix and the Spire
premise: Sebastian Okonkwo, youngest of the Hollowmere guild, has lived his whole life in a valley where magic cannot follow — the only safe place left for the giftless and gifted alike. When crown hunters breach the valley chasing rumors of a living spire-heart, Sebastian flees with Beatrix, the guild's exiled founder whose magic was severed decades ago, and discovers the secret she carries: the spire's dormant core, which could either restore magic to the world or reignite the war that burned it once before. Hunted across a kingdom turning on its own, Sebastian must choose between surrendering the core to save his captured guildmates and unleashing a power no one can control. In the end he shatters the core rather than let either side claim it, scattering magic into the people themselves — and finds that belonging was never the valley, but the ones who walked out of it with him.
about_author: J. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval guild records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about found families and institutions that outlive their purpose.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet Hollowmere, the guild's dying valley refuge, through Sebastian's chores and quiet resentments; he's never crossed the wardline and doesn't believe he ever will. Beatrix watches him with an old grief he can't name. Beat: longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Crown's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A royal crier at the valley's edge announces a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, offering bounty and pardon to informers. The guild elders argue about whether to hide or scatter; Beatrix goes silent. Beat: the safe world cracks open.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Buried
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, first time. She reveals to Sebastian that the valley's ward is powered by the spire-core she stole and hid forty years ago — and that the crown's hunters are looking for it, not just for people. Beat: the mentor becomes a fugitive.

chapters.title: The Wardline Breaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Hunters breach the valley using a captured guildmate's testimony. In the chaos, Beatrix unearths the core; it flares, killing a hunter, and Sebastian's own dormant gift wakes for the first time. They flee across the wardline together. Beat: terror and terrible exhilaration.

chapters.title: Roads Without Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The pair travel incognito through a border town where neighbors are already informing on neighbors. Sebastian learns to smother his gift; Beatrix teaches him the old guild disciplines. Beat: first fragile trust between them.

chapters.title: The Informer's Price
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix recognizes a former guild sister now working for the crown and must decide whether to silence her. She chooses mercy; the sister betrays them anyway within a day. Beat: the cost of mercy in a lawless time.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They reach a waystation and find it burned — the crown is burning every site with guild history. Sebastian realizes his entire heritage is being erased, and his grief curdles into anger. Beat: from survival to purpose.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Gifts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In a smuggler's market they meet Odile, a neutral broker who maps gifted people for whoever pays. She offers passage in exchange for a reading of the core — and warns that the crown's chief hunter, Veyra, never loses a quarry. Beat: the world is bigger and more compromised than the valley taught.

chapters.title: Veyra
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV, first time. The crown's hunter interrogates the captured guildmates and deduces the core's location from Beatrix's old habits. She is not cruel; she genuinely believes magic must be extinguished for peace. Beat: an antagonist with a case.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sheltering in a flooded ruin, Sebastian practices with his gift and nearly drowns a village child by accident. Beatrix saves them both and finally tells him the full story of the ancient war the core once fueled. Beat: the gift is not a blessing; it is a responsibility.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Odile's price turns out to be the core itself, to sell to the highest bidder. Beatrix negotiates a lie — passage in exchange for a decoy — knowing it will make Odile an enemy. Beat: Beatrix's ruthlessness surfaces, and Sebastian sees his mentor clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Guild That Was
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They pass through the guild's ruined motherhouse. Sebastian finds his own name pre-entered in a membership ledger decades old — Beatrix chose him before he was born. Beat: belonging as inheritance, and its weight.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra's riders ambush the pair at a river crossing; Beatrix is captured covering Sebastian's escape with the core. Veyra offers Beatrix pardon in exchange for the core's location — and begins to suspect Beatrix wants to be caught. Beat: the hunt inverts.

chapters.title: Alone with the Heart of the World
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Alone for the first time, Sebastian must decide: trade the core for Beatrix, or finish what she started. He hears the core speak — or believes he does — and understands it wants to be used. Beat: temptation, isolation, resolve.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Greyford
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian walks into Veyra's camp offering the core for Beatrix and the guildmates. Veyra agrees — but Sebastian secretly plans to destroy it at the exchange. Beat: the hero becomes the one taking a hostage of a kind: the future itself.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Betrayed by Beatrix's decoy, Odile sells the exchange's location to a rebel faction of the gifted who want the core as a weapon. All three forces now converge on Greyford. Beat: no side is clean; the war is already reigniting.

chapters.title: Greyford
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The exchange erupts into a three-way battle: crown, rebels, and Sebastian. Beatrix breaks free using a last scrap of severed magic; Sebastian reaches the core as rebels and hunters close in. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Shattering
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. Rather than let anyone claim it, Sebastian pours his own gift into the core and shatters it. Magic bursts outward into everyone present — hunter, rebel, bystander alike. Beatrix is gravely wounded holding off Veyra. Beat: the terrible, liberating climax; the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: What the Crown Cannot Hunt
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. In the aftermath, Veyra confronts the collapse of her mission: you cannot hunt a gift that lives in everyone. She lets Sebastian go, or perhaps simply has no order that fits what happened. Beat: the law meets justice outside it, and blinks.

chapters.title: Ashes and Seeds
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Beatrix survives, diminished; the guildmates are freed. Magic is now common, small, and ungovernable — the valley's ward is gone forever. The survivors argue about what the guild should become. Beat: grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Spire's Remnant
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix and Sebastian return to Hollowmere and find villagers already using small magics, frightened and free. Beatrix formally dissolves the old guild's secrecy and re-founds it as something open. Beat: the mentor passes the torch fully.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Spire
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing. On the ruined spire's foundations, Sebastian teaches the valley's first open class in the new guild. Beatrix watches, finally at peace. He understands the spire was never the stone — it was the people who kept the secret, and then the courage to stop keeping it. Beat: belonging, earned.
